violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.profiles has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.profiles FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: Policy expression does not reference any column of the table
violations.message: Policy 'nobody' on public.profiles does not reference any column of the table. The predicate is purely session-state — every row is admitted or denied based on configuration alone. Add a row-level condition (e.g. tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant')).

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.profiles is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: Policy clause is constant false
violations.message: Policy 'nobody' on public.profiles has USING (false), which denies every row. Express denial at the GRANT layer instead — `REVOKE ALL ON TABLE public.profiles FROM <role>` is clearer than a deny-all policy that makes the table look RLS-protected when it's actually denying every row.

violations.title: RLS-enabled table has no write-side policy
violations.message: Table public.profiles has RLS enabled and 1 policy, but every policy is FOR SELECT — no policy covers INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE. With RLS enforced and no write-side policy, writes by non-owner roles are denied: INSERT raises a row-violates-policy error, while UPDATE and DELETE silently affect zero rows. If the table is meant to be read-only for these roles (writes done by a table-owning or BYPASSRLS role), allowlist it as 'public.profiles' in [lint.rules.SEC022]. Otherwise add a policy covering the write commands — a FOR ALL policy, or a FOR INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE policy.

violations.title: RLS table has a principal column no policy scopes by
violations.message: Table public.profiles has RLS enabled and a policy, but no policy references the principal column(s) 'owner_id'. Rows are scoped by whatever the policies do key on (often tenant), so users that share that scope can see each other's rows. If this table holds per-user-private data, add a predicate keying on 'owner_id'; if it is intentionally shared (a catalogue, a tenant-wide settings table), add it to [lint.rules.SEC027].allowlist.
